title: runtime: a package export silently drops a whole metadata type when its per-package read throws, so the export (and the whole-deployment bundle) can be thinner with no error
body:
domain:server#4 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbacSXJQqAztgt4UMrS

Filing gate: ① an out-of-scope finding of the #28914 dev (os-dev-report 6594757585), escalated by the contract review of PR #29755 (record 6594891654, ③ item 6). Filed by `domain:server` seat 4. ⛔ Not a claim. Suggested-grade: p2 (an export that reads complete but is not; the exit-right promise depends on it).

## What happens

`assemblePackageManifest` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`, the per-type loop near line 3345 on `origin/main` `3eeb81d19`) reads each exportable type through `protocol.getMetaItemsPerPackage` (or `getMetaItems`). The whole read sits in a `try { … } catch { continue; }` whose comment says "Unknown/unsupported type for this runtime — skip". So **any** failure of that read, not only an unknown type, drops the whole type from the export. `GET /packages/:id/export` then answers 200 with that collection missing, and the new whole-deployment bundle (`GET /packages/export`, #28914) inherits the same silent hole per entry.

A reinstall from such an export lands without that type, and nothing tells the operator. Source reading only; not yet reproduced through a door.

## Governing text

- #28914's declaration (PR #29100, `PackageExportBundleSchema`): the bundle is "whole or absent". PR #29755 honours that per package (a throw outside the loop or a `null` assembly fails the read, naming the package), but a per-type failure inside the loop is invisible to it.
- The one-producer rule from the same declaration: the bundle composes the per-package export, so the fix belongs in `assemblePackageManifest`, not in the bundle.

## Wanted

1. Tell an unknown or unsupported type (skip, as today) apart from a failed read of a known type (fail the export, naming the package and the type).
2. Both the per-package export and the bundle then refuse instead of answering a thinner body. Decide the status by the existing refusal family of the export route.
3. Pins: an unknown type is still skipped; a throwing read of a known type fails `GET /packages/:id/export` and `GET /packages/export`, naming both.

Serial: after PR #29755 (same file and function).

Dedupe: searched `assemblePackageManifest catch continue`, `package export silently drops type`, `export thinner`; nearest is #28914 (the bundle). **New.**

Links back: #28914, PR #29755, PR #29100, #28409.
